g.text: SalesEasy: public-data lookup, one request at a time
Explicit barcode search. Real records are context, never verified outlet stock.
1. Browser submits barcode
POST /api/products/lookup
2. Parse body + strict Zod validation
Only barcode; remove spaces and hyphens
GTIN-8 / UPC-A / EAN-13 / GTIN-14
Validate digits and checksum before network
Invalid input -> HTTP 400
No source requests; display input error
3. Read both fixed HTTPS origins in parallel
Promise.allSettled: independent outcomes
Custom application User-Agent
Each source: 8s timeout, 15-min revalidation
Read-only; no provider key or DeepSeek call
4a. Open Food Facts
GET /api/v3.6/product/{barcode}.json
Read name, brand, pack, country tags, modified time
404 means not found; other failures unavailable
4b. Open Prices
GET /api/v1/prices
Exact barcode; date <= today; newest first; max 8
Read amount, currency, date, store and proof
5. Validate each source response
Product barcode must match request
Drop mismatched or future price observations
Keep provenance; missing fields stay null
Never infer outlet stock or convert currencies
6. Return validated lookup JSON + status
Product: found / not_found / unavailable
Prices: available / none / unavailable
200 for usable or partial results
503 when both sources are unavailable
7. Browser validates + displays the result
Product identity and original pack size
Dated prices, location, currency and source links
Warn when observations are older than 90 days
Stock on hand = Unknown
Source failure remains visible; no silent success
Response context and limits
Source IDs, URLs, record dates, lookup time
Cached records can be older than lookup time
Community contributions may be inaccurate
No price-match approval or inventory join
Client wait cap: 20s; Cancel stops waiting
Errors are safe: no raw upstream bodies or secrets. Unexpected failures return a generic HTTP 503 error.
No lookup result is sent to DeepSeek. A historical price or product listing does not establish current stock.
